messages:
tara: Heads-up — we saw a sustained spike in long-context requests over the last 3h. Per-GPU tokens/sec on the p4d pool is down ~18%. Need to re-evaluate headroom for next week (holiday traffic + marketing campaign).
liam: Which metric are you looking at? aggregate tokens/sec or per-model?
devon: quick grab from prom:
```
model          tokens_per_sec  concurrent_reqs  gpu_util
redwood-rlhf   58k             420              78%
long-context   42k             180              84%
small-quant    120k            300              65%
pool (p4d)     72k avg         900 total        79%
```
jules: sounds like model-mix shift -> more long-context churn. That lowers batching efficiency (shorter coalesced batches). We should consider routing a % to the quantized variant during spikes.
tara: If tokens/sec is down 18% on avg, what's the expected GPU-hour delta for next week at our projected volume? Need ballpark for finance.
liam: rough calc: current baseline = 72k tokens/sec per-GPU. If demand constant, 18% drop -> effective 59k tps. To keep throughput we need ~22% more GPUs. So if we run 250 GPUs normally -> ~305 GPUs => +55 GPUs.
devon: GPU-hours: +55 GPUs * 24 * 7 = 9240 GPU-hours for the week (if sustained). That's worst-case.
ops-qa: ok that's material. Any cheaper mitigations before we scale?
jules: two levers: 1) prefix caching for common prompts (we measured ~10-15% tokens gain in test) 2) dynamic fallback: route 20-30% of non-sensitive requests to small-quant model which has much better tps.
tara: prefix cache + 25% fallback sounds promising. What's the quality hit?
jules: in evals, fallback increased latency slightly for a subset but P0 metrics stayed within threshold. Quality drop ~3% top-level score on long-context-specific evals. We can A/B for 48h.
liam: note: cross-region routing to us-west will add ~5-10ms and we already have limited spare capacity in eu-west. APAC capacity limited for p4d next month (quota requests pending).
infra-bot: [capacity-plan-checker] auto-scan: projected weekly GPU-hour shortfall if no action = 8.6k-10.2k. Recommended policy: enable fallback route (20%) + pre-warm + cache.
ops-qa: cost delta estimate?
liam: back-of-envelope: $3.2 / GPU-hour average for committed p4d rate -> 9240 * 3.2 = ~$29.6k extra for worst-case week. With fallback+cache we expect to cut that to ~3k-7k incremental.
tara: action items:
- liam: flip on 20% fallback route for non-sensitive traffic (canary 2% -> 10% -> 20%) by EOD.
- devon: run a sim overnight with current arrival distribution + long-context weight up 30%, capture tokens/sec and required GPUs.
- jules: implement prefix cache experiment and attach eval deck.
- ops-qa: run cost model update for finance.
liam: I'll post canary plan in #eng-releases and tag infra on rollout.
devon: sim job scheduled at 23:30 UTC, will share logs and the sim script. snippet: 
```
# sim job args
--arrival-profile=prod-weighted
--scale-long-context=1.3
--run-duration=2h
--output=/tmp/sim/177250_sim.json
```
tara: perfect. Please @channel if sim shows >15% additional GPU need. Also link to forecast doc: https://internal.redwood.ai/infra/forecasts/2026-holiday (added notes).
liam: noted. keeping an eye. :eyes:
ops-qa: thanks all — will prep a short finance blip for tomorrow's sync. :+1:
